chunks: My father, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan all narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman al-Naysaburi, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Yamani narrated to us from Mani' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Yunus ibn 'ibn 'Abd Allah [al-Rahman], from Qudamah ibn Malik, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever visits al-Husayn anticipating [reward from God], without arrogance and extravagance, and without showing off and seeking fame, his sins will be purified just as a garment is purified with water, so no impurity remains on it. And for him is recorded, with every step, a Hajj, and with every time he raises a foot, an 'Umrah.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and conditions for visiting Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith highlights the theological significance of Ziyarah as an act of worship that expiates sins through the metaphor of washing a garment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and purifying power of the Ahl al-Bayt. It further elevates the status of the visitor by equating each step to a complete Hajj and 'Umrah, underscoring the immense spiritual merit attached to commemorating the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.).
